clues: A 15th-century citadel of a mountain empire, set on a ridge 2,430 metres above sea level, with a river looping round the cliffs below it.
It lies high in the Andes, about 80 km north-west of the empire's former capital.

reveal.explanation: Machu Picchu is a 15th-century Inca citadel on a mountain ridge at 2,430 metres, about 80 km north-west of Cusco, the former Inca capital, with the Urubamba River below. It is estimated to have been built around 1450 and is believed to have served as an estate for the Inca emperor Pachacuti.

sources.excerpt: Machu Picchu (13°09′48″S 72°32′44″W) is a 15th-century Inca citadel located in the Eastern Cordillera of southern Peru on a mountain ridge at 2,430 meters (7,970 ft). It is located about 80 kilometers (50 miles) northwest of Cusco, above the Urubamba River. Estimated to be built around 1450, it is believed to have served as an estate for the Inca emperor Pachacuti.
